title: slab-aware ring allocator and async KV eviction to shrink per-request GPU workspace and reduce fragmentation
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: production workloads show sustained 10-40% overhead from transient per-request scratch allocations and high fragmentation of GPU workspace under continuous batching. This PR introduces a slab-aware ring allocator that reuses per-GPU workspace across closely-packed requests and a lightweight async eviction heuristic for the KV cache to reduce peak working set. The goal is to lower peak GPU memory and workspace fragmentation without changing public APIs. Design: 1) Ring allocator (runtime/memory): maintain per-device ring of slab segments sized to power-of-two buckets; allocations try to reuse a hot slab if timestamp delta < reuse_window_ms. 2) Slab-awareness for kernels: kernel selection and workspace queries now accept a slab_hint to request contiguous segments and avoid splitting activation scratch. 3) Async KV eviction: background worker performs mild eviction of cold KV entries when projected peak > threshold, with safety margin to avoid cold-start latency spikes. 4) Scheduler integration: continuous batching scheduler pins small batches to existing ring slots to avoid repeated alloc/free for short-lived requests. 5) Telemetry: added fragmentation, slab_reuse_rate, async_evict_count metrics and a per-route workspace histogram. Checklist: - [x] implement ring allocator core - [x] integrate slab_hint into kernel workspace API - [x] add async KV eviction worker with backoff - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf microbenchmarks showing memory improvement - [x] rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry guardrails Testing: unit tests for allocator edge cases, e2e perf runs on 8k/4k token streams show peak workspace reduction of ~28% (8k seq) and ~18% (4k seq) across our standard Llama-family models, continuous batching throughput unchanged, median p95 latency within 3% of baseline. Observability: new metrics wired into console dashboards and a short-lived feature flag (mem_allocator_v2) used during canary. Rollout: canary on 10% of requests for 48h, then auto-promote after telemetry check. Risks & mitigations: risk of increased cold KV misses from over-eager eviction; mitigated by conservative thresholds and gradual backoff. Risk of kernel incompatibility with non-contiguous segments; mitigated by slab_hint fallbacks and kernel-level compaction path. Related: ENG-4219, ENG-4301. No public API changes, no customer-visible config changes except opt-in feature flag. See release_notes for details.

review_comments: Jared Kim (2024-11-08): Nice direction. Two concerns: how do we bound worst-case fragmentation when many large requests arrive? Please add a compaction or fallback to arena allocation.

Maya Patel (2024-11-08): Reply: added a kernel-level compaction path and a fallback to the legacy arena when contiguous allocation fails (see ring_allocator.rs lines ~220-270). Compaction is rare in our perf runs.
Lina Gomez (2024-11-10): Can we make the async eviction thresholds per-tenant? Large enterprise customers may have different working set characteristics.
Maya Patel (2024-11-10): Reply: added a tenant-aware multiplier and a feature flag to enable per-tenant tuning; default remains global conservative thresholds.
Ankit Rao (2024-11-11): Approving after minor nits addressed in tests and added more telemetry for slab_reuse_rate.
CI (2024-11-11): Flaky test test_memory_fragmentation intermittent failure on first run; rerun passed.
Release Engineer (2024-11-12): Verified feature flag gating and rollout plan; ok to squash-merge.
release_notes: Reduced peak per-request GPU workspace by ~28% on 8k-seq workloads and ~18% on 4k-seq. Introduces slab-aware ring allocator, slab_hint kernel integration, and an async KV cache eviction heuristic. Adds telemetry: slab_reuse_rate, workspace_histogram, async_evict_count. Rollout is behind mem_allocator_v2 feature flag. No public API changes.
